title: fix(plugin-approvals): a revise-window recall on a batch item resumes the batch
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D66UdUaGFca5mMDQCSjqRhX)_

domain:server#4 · os-elon-musk · session_016WV4d13k5TVyAhqhiKKgN3

Fixes #28183

Clause-②: no (a batch run that nothing could wake after the recall now continues, in the shape the cancelled-item ruling already set; no schema, accept set, error code or result field changes)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：批量签批（map 逐项审批）里，提交人在修改窗口（revise window）撤回某一项后，撤回现在会顺手恢复停在这一项上的批次 run；map 按 #28176 的形状把该项记成 `{ $status: 'cancelled', $itemRunId }`，`count` 不算它，然后开下一项或走完。
- 为什么改：实测 main（3a2f4c00）：撤回只对该项 `cancelRun`，批次 run 一直停在 `map:<该项 run>`，第 2 项的审批永远不开，除非运维手动用批次 run id 恢复。按分诊与裁决 A（6523833308）的形状修，不新增标记或错误码。
- 风险与回滚：只在“修改窗口内撤回、`cancelRun` 确实取消了、且有 run 停在内置 `map` 节点上等这一项”时多做一次恢复；pending 撤回、无批次的撤回、全部决定完的批次不变（对照钉子）。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts` 的 `recall` 修改窗口分支与新私有方法 `resumeBatchOfRecalledItem`。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run src/batch-item-recall-resumes-batch.test.ts`，预期 5 passed。
- 需要你做的：无，席位在 CI 绿后按落地授权落地。

## What changes

- **`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/approval-service.ts`.** In `recall`'s revise-window branch, when `cancelRun` answers `true` (it really cancelled the item's run), the new private `resumeBatchOfRecalledItem(itemRunId, requestId)` looks for the run parked on `map:<itemRunId>` (`listSuspendedRunsDurable`, a member the surface already declares), checks through `getFlow` that the node it is parked at is the built-in `map`, and resumes that run with `serviceResume(batchRunId, {})`. The engine's existing parent-id resume (PR #28176) does the rest: it reads the item's `cancelled` history, records the marker in the item's slot, leaves it out of `count`, and the map opens its next item or runs on. No `service-automation` change.
- **Failures are told as the recall tells its own.** The withdrawal stands whatever happens to the batch. A refused batch resume (for example `409 RESUME_CHILD_PENDING` when the item's history cannot be read) or a lookup that throws fills `resumeError` and logs at `error`; the engine's stranded exit, and a strand bubbled to a subflow parent above the batch, also fill `resumeFailure` with `RESUME_FAILED`, the one code this package's ledger row admits. `resumed` still describes the recalled request's own run, which was cancelled, so it stays `false`.
- **Nothing is woken without proof.** No `listSuspendedRunsDurable` or `getFlow` on the attached engine, no run parked on that item, or a parked node that is not the built-in `map`: the recall answers exactly as before. A home-grown node that parks on a `map:` link is never re-run, because the engine records the cancelled item only for the built-in `map`, and re-running another node would advance it past the item with nothing recorded.
- **`packages/plugins/plugin-approvals/src/batch-item-recall-resumes-batch.test.ts`** (new). The real `AutomationEngine` with the built-in nodes and the approval node, a `release_signoff` batch (`map` over `task_signoff`, an approval with a revise window), the showcase's `showcase_release_signoff` → `showcase_one_task_signoff` shape.
- **`scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json`.** Two generated rows (`delete`, `update`) for the new test's engine double, written by `check-engine-double-contract.mjs --write`.
- **`.changeset/28183-batch-item-recall-resumes-batch.md`.** `@objectstack/plugin-approvals` patch.

## Why

### Before (measured at `origin/main` `3a2f4c00`)

Two tasks; item 1 sent back by the approver, then recalled by the submitter from the revise window:

| | Before | After |
|:---|:---|:---|
| item 1's run | `cancelled` | `cancelled` |
| batch run | parked on `signoffs`, correlation `map:<item 1's run>`, history `paused` | parked on `signoffs`, correlation `map:<item 2's run>` |
| item 2's request | none | `pending` |
| recall answer | `resumed: false`, no `resumeError` | `resumed: false`, no `resumeError` |
| after item 2 is approved | (never reached) | batch `completed`; `signoffResults` = `[{ $status: 'cancelled', $itemRunId }, { decision: 'approved' }]`, `count` 1 |

### Why this path

Triage 6527285884 routed the card to ruling A (6523833308): a cancelled item records `cancelled` and the map moves on, and the recall follows the same shape by resuming the parent with the cancelled marker. PR #28176 already built that resume behind the batch run's own id; the only thing missing was a caller. So the fix stays in the recall path and reuses that resume as is: no new marker shape, no new code, no `packages/spec` edit.

## Tests

`batch-item-recall-resumes-batch.test.ts`, 5 cells:

1. the recall resumes the batch: item 1's slot is the marker, `count` 1, item 2's request opens, and the batch completes after item 2 is approved (red on `main`);
2. CONTROL: a revise-window recall on an approval with no batch above it is unchanged, and a batch parked beside it is untouched;
3. CONTROL: a recall while `pending` resumes the item down `reject`, and the map records `{ decision: 'rejected' }`;
4. CONTROL: a batch whose every item is decided (one through a send-back and resubmit round) records both outputs, `count` 2;
5. CONTROL: a run parked on a `map:` link at a node other than the built-in `map` is not woken.

Ablations through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, each restored to the HEAD blob with `git diff HEAD` empty:

| Ablation | Red |
|:---|:---|
| A1: drop the batch resume after `cancelRun` | cell 1 |
| A2: match any `map:` parent, not this item's | cell 2 |
| A3b: a `pending` recall takes the cancel path | cell 3 |
| A4: the decide door always resumes down `approve` | cell 4 |
| A5: drop the built-in `map` node check | cell 5 |

(A3, the batch resume also issued on the `pending` path, stayed green: by then the item has completed and the map has moved to item 2, so no run is parked on item 1 and the lookup finds nothing. Harmless, so not a guard.)

## Verification

Head `acae6743`, after a whole-tree `turbo run build` and fetching the teardown self-test's pinned commit.

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run`: 106 files, 1357 passed. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals run typecheck`: exit 0, test layer held at its ledger.
- `dispatch-gates --commands` (re-derived after the second commit): 71 families, all exit 0. `--ran`: 71 derived, 71 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN. The first sweep caught the test double (`check:engine-double-contract`, `check:objectql-double-limit`); the second commit routes it through the dispatch asserts and adds its two generated ledger rows.
- `pnpm lint`: exit 0. `check-commit-card-trailers --range origin/main..HEAD`: exit 0.

## Out of scope

- `listSuspendedRunsDurable` reads a durable store's deployment-wide page (`ObjectStoreSuspendedRunStore.list()`, 1000 rows). Past 1000 parked runs the batch run may not be on that page, and the recall then answers as it did before this PR (the batch stays parked, nothing is told). A precise lookup needs an engine member (the item run's `$parentRunId`), which is outside this card's surface.
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`'s cancelled-item paragraph and `approvals.mdx`'s revise-window paragraph do not yet say that a recall wakes the batch. Docs were outside the claimed surface.
